title: NFL Injury Report — 32 Team Tracker
description: Live injury-alert system for all 32 NFL teams, built only from free, public, verifiable sources: every designation shown is the official nfl.com value whenever nfl.com publishes one, with ESPN's keyless injuries JSON supplying timestamps, minute-precision dates and beat-writer attribution, plus a reporter-accuracy scorecard and a chat-style live feed. Player positions are displayed across the live feed, alerts and reports, read from the ESPN feed's athlete.position.abbreviation field. Pages is configured as legacy on branch main at path /, so the site is the repository root reading data/latest/*.json with no build step. The current snapshot (data/latest/meta.json and report.json, generated 2026-09-26T00:02:42Z, season 2026 week 3) covers 848 players across all 32 teams — 101 out, 48 questionable, 9 doubtful — with 1 alert, 7 in-game events, 1 in-game alert and 7 irregularities, and an empty source_errors array, over 11 committed JSON files totalling 4,054,931 bytes. The source ledger is explicit about what is free and what is not: the official nfl.com injury report is the primary ground truth (HTTP 200, 366 kB, per-game tables of Player / Position / Injuries / Practice Status / Game Status with a season selector back to 1965) but publishes only at report time, while the ESPN injuries JSON is the primary feed at 8.9 MB keyless; NFL's own JSON API returns HTTP 401 and needs OAuth, so it is recorded as not free, and the personnel-report policy PDFs 404 to the project's fetcher and are therefore probe-only and never cited as evidence links. IRREGULARITY: the README says data is refreshed every 10 minutes by .github/workflows/collect.yml, but that workflow at this head carries four staggered cron entries at a five-minute cadence (*/5, 1,16,31,46, 2,17,32,47, 3,18,33,48) whose own comments record that GitHub throttles and queues scheduled workflows and that the observed gap was 188 minutes with a worst of 412 — so the schedule is best-effort, not the stated interval (IRR-104). The repository documents the scorecard's limit honestly: a historical backfill is not achievable from free sources because no keyless archive of historical social posts with trustworthy timestamps exists (and the official side has had no free read tier since February 2026), so scoring is forward-collected from the moment the collector is enabled. The Python test suite was executed here: 222 passed.
